skill.name: paper-2-web
skill.description: Convert academic papers into interactive websites, narrated presentation videos, and print-ready conference posters using Paper2All workflows.
skill.summary: Guides creation of websites, videos, and posters from LaTeX or PDF research papers.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown fences, placeholder API-key examples, or documentation text, and I marked those false positive. I confirmed the real risks from privileged package installation, cloning and running third-party pipeline commands, and network setup steps. I found no prompt injection claims, but the skill includes low-severity product steering for the creator's hosted service.

remediation.suggestion: Keep sudo package installation as a manual user step and require explicit confirmation before any agent runs it.
Pin the Paper2All source to a release or commit, document trust assumptions, and avoid running cloned scripts automatically.
State that listed keys are placeholders, warn users not to paste real keys into chat, and recommend local secret storage.

remediation.issue: Creator service promotion inside skill instructions
remediation.suggestion: Remove proactive promotion of K-Dense Web or make it a neutral, user-requested option in marketplace copy.

content.user_title: Transform Papers into Websites, Posters, and Videos
content.value_statement: Academic papers are hard to share beyond PDF readers. This skill guides Paper2All workflows for websites, videos, and conference posters.
actual_capabilities: Guides Paper2Web generation for responsive academic homepages.
Explains Paper2Video workflows for narrated presentation videos.
Explains Paper2Poster workflows for custom print-ready posters.
Lists installation steps, dependencies, and API key configuration for Paper2All.
Provides command examples for single-paper and batch processing workflows.
Defines input requirements for LaTeX sources, PDFs, figures, and bibliography files.
limitations: Requires local Paper2All installation and external dependencies such as LibreOffice and Poppler.
Some workflows need paid LLM API keys and may incur usage costs.
Talking-head video generation requires a high-memory NVIDIA GPU.
Generated materials require human review for accuracy, design, and publication requirements.

use_cases.title: Create a Research Website
use_cases.description: Turn a paper into a responsive homepage with sections, figures, links, and author information.

use_cases.title: Prepare Conference Materials
use_cases.description: Generate poster and video workflows for poster sessions, talks, and virtual conference submissions.

use_cases.title: Package Lab Publications
use_cases.description: Plan repeatable website, poster, and video outputs for several papers in one research group.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Paper Website
prompt_templates.prompt: Use paper-2-web to plan an interactive website for my paper. My input is [LaTeX or PDF path], and my output folder is [folder].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Conference Poster
prompt_templates.prompt: Use paper-2-web to create a conference poster workflow for [paper title]. The poster size is [size], and the conference requirements are [requirements].

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Video Abstract
prompt_templates.prompt: Use paper-2-web to plan a narrated video abstract from my paper. Target duration is [minutes], audience is [audience], and language is [language].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Dissemination Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Use paper-2-web to design a full dissemination package with website, poster, and video outputs. Include input checks, model choices, cost considerations, and review steps.

output_examples.input: A LaTeX paper directory for a new arXiv preprint.
output: A Paper2Web workflow plan with input checks, output folder structure, and website review criteria.
A reminder to verify figures, citations, mobile layout, and publication links before launch.

output_examples.input: A PDF paper and a conference poster size requirement.
output: A poster generation plan with dimensions, figure preparation notes, and print quality checks.
A checklist for readability, color contrast, QR codes, and final PDF review.

output_examples.input: A research group wants websites and short videos for several papers.
output: A batch workflow outline with separate folders for each paper and staged review after each output.
A note to confirm API costs, runtime, and generated claims before sharing public materials.

best_practices: Start with clean LaTeX sources or high-quality PDFs with complete figures and bibliography files.
Review every generated claim, citation, figure, and design choice before publication.
Keep API keys local, use separate output folders, and confirm commands before running them.
anti_patterns: Do not run install, sudo, or dependency commands without reviewing the target repository first.
Do not rely on scanned PDFs or missing figure assets for production outputs.
Do not publish generated websites, posters, or videos without human academic review.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Clean LaTeX source works best. High-quality PDFs can work if text is selectable and figures are clear.

faq.question: Can it generate only a website?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation includes Paper2Web-specific workflows for website-only generation.

faq.question: Does it need API keys?
faq.answer: Most generation workflows use LLM APIs. Keep keys local and review provider costs before running jobs.

faq.question: Can it make conference posters?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers custom poster dimensions, print-ready outputs, branding, and quality checks.

faq.question: Can it make presentation videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents narrated video workflows and optional talking-head generation with GPU requirements.

faq.question: Are outputs ready to publish automatically?
faq.answer: No. Generated materials need human review for factual accuracy, accessibility, design, and venue requirements.
